caption: The drawing depicts a single eagle with its wings fully spread, facing toward the right side of the image. The eagle appears detailed, with individual feathers rendered carefully on both the wings and the body. The eagle’s head is held high with the beak slightly open, showing a prominent curve and hooked tip. Its talons are not visible as its lower body and legs are perched on what appears to be a cluster of rounded, cloud-like forms. The entire image is shaded in tones of black and gray, with no other colors present. The background is plain and unshaded, which highlights the detailed, shaded figure of the eagle. In the lower left corner, the name “H. BADER” is written in small capital letters.
title: Eagle
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
